title: bn254-gt-dlp: gated tag-walk rho with a two-level signed tag (120 instructions per step), expected work

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and z=g^x in the protected BN254 target group GT, the algorithm in proof.md recovers x (for z=1: x=0) with success at least 0.39, as algorithmic probability over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, under the disclosed heuristics H1 (an opened run of the algorithm as specified, caps included, makes at most 107/100 times sqrt(pi r m/(2(m-1))) walk steps in expectation, m=6) and H2 (the run's expected counts of steps at each tag level, exits and reports are at most those of an explicit idealized process in which the read coordinate at every fresh step, one at an element not equal to a p^(2i)-Frobenius image of an earlier evaluated element, is a fresh uniform residue, and the run makes at most 2^93 non-fresh steps in expectation, each charged in full), supported by proved two-level tag lemmas, algebra on the pinned constants, a census of the read coordinate over a whole toy GT and full-algorithm toy runs. Before any other work the algorithm reads one fresh 64-bit coin u and opens the run only when u < K, K = 7208315804938894124, the least integer for which the opened share of runs times the supported success of an opened run reaches 0.39; a closed run costs 64 instructions and is counted as a failure. An opened run finds x by a sequential distinguished-point Pollard rho walk in GT with 6 multipliers g^c z^d: the next multiplier is read from stored coordinate 6 of the current element (multiplied by a primitive sixth root of unity by the p^2 Frobenius), the multipliers are redrawn when two are related by a p^(2i) Frobenius power, a step computes a 64-bit level-1 tag as the inner product of 60 signed 51-bit digits with 60 table words and uses it only when it certifies the exact selector, else a level-2 tag from 60 more words and signed high products, else evaluates the element exactly (proof.md section 2); the table holds every product of at most 1,024 multipliers, one Fp12 product re-bases the element every 1,024 steps, distinguished elements (90 bits) go to an ordered store keyed by the whole element, and g^x=z is checked before output; it continues until it finds x or a counter reaches its cap. The score is an expectation: the expected total computation over the same uniform challenges and fresh coins is at most 2^118.828325 target-group-operation equivalents (scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by C=20,000). It is not a bound on every run: on every run the total computation is at most 2^131.353421 equivalents, enforced by counters (a trip budget of 1,025 per call of the step loop, a 3-word exit counter compared with its cap at every exit, 2^50 walk starts, 2^50 reports, 16 recoveries). Prices are executed instruction counts of generated AArch64 programs: 120 instructions per walk step, 177 more for a step that needs the second tag level, and 15,619 per exit from the step loop (one Fp12 product of 13,843 with the label additions, digits and counters, plus a stated allowance). Both totals include the gate, all input checks, constants, the table construction, fresh coins (16 instructions per 64-bit word), walk starts, reports, store operations, recoveries, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^61.353586 bytes in one address space with 64-bit pointers; preprocessing is at most 2^56.249959 equivalents and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Nothing is amortised over other targets, and no prior acceptance, submission or score is a premise. Analytic exploratory claim: no production-size run, not a finite-field sieve estimate.

experiments.purpose: Generate and execute the priced AArch64 programs (Fp multiply/add/sub, Fp12 product, the two-level step loop on real windows of a real walk, the re-base with its digits, window constants and counters on both sides of both caps, both sides of both certificate thresholds, random-word entries on the level-2 path, the trip budget, the callee-saved registers) against big-integer arithmetic and print executed counts; check both tag lemmas and the certified-selector corollary on production-size values and the read coordinate under the Frobenius powers; recompute every ledger integer, the gate constant K (and that K - 1 fails), the expected and every-run totals and the score; run the complete algorithm of proof.md to its output in the BN-family toy field q=p(-15), r'=r(-15), compare it with a plain reference walk, and count the read coordinate over the whole toy group for q=p(-7). Toy results are evidence at toy scale only.
